chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no harm in the Qimah (payment in kind) for Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr).

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.الْقِيمَةِ: Payment in kind or specific goods (as opposed to currency)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay Zakat al-Fitr in kind (Qimah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirming the validity of paying Zakat al-Fitr in monetary value (*Qimah*) rather than solely in specific foodstuffs. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for allowing flexibility in fulfilling the obligation, accommodating varying economic conditions and local customs. It reflects the pragmatic application of divine law, ensuring the poor receive the equivalent benefit regardless of the medium of exchange.
